title: The Forty-Four-Minute Vote, the Pure Soul, and the Air Elemental
subtitle: In Which Waluigi Runs the Pond Footage Without Letting It Invent a Ghost
filed: 1 Aethel, 1040 BF — after the session account; no clock recorded
pullQuote: A ghost-shaped problem, an elemental on the reading, and one rope that is no longer doing its job. WAH!
standfirst: Waluigi has the Purple Town account on the projector, and the reel starts with forty-four minutes of voting before it reaches a pond, an apparition, and a Toad who has the wrong Speaker in mind. He can pause the footage to yell; he cannot use the pause button to turn a claim into a fact or to show what happens after the account stops.

sections.heading: FORTY-FOUR MINUTES OF VOTING AND RIVERS GETS NO SAY
sections.body:
Waluigi starts the projector at the vote. Forty-four minutes pass while the group decides what to do next, and the assignments come out in two directions: Remi is sent to emergency fortifications for the Stonecutters; Archie and Markop take the reported hauntings. The tape gives those jobs and does not give the Stonecutters' position or Remi's destination. Waluigi is already pointing at the blank space. No, he will not draw a map there.

Speaker Rivers asks whether he gets a say. Markop tells him no. Archie offers a different arrangement: Rivers can watch him act and judge him by what he does. Rivers says perhaps he can win Archie over; Archie says he can try. Waluigi freezes the frame on that exchange. Rivers has a voice, a promise, and no vote in these assignments. Those are not the same thing, however much everyone would like the scene to tidy itself up.

Then the party reaches Purple Town, in the suburbs of the Regal Capital, with its airship nearby. A man named Cornbury approaches and says he works for the Order of the Regal Lion. He asks whether they have come to expel evil spirits. Archie corrects the job description: investigate first, condemn later. Waluigi gives Archie one approving nod and immediately takes it back when Markop agrees so quickly that the screen barely has time to change.

Cornbury brings up goblins; Archie recalls crossing paths with one but cannot place exactly where. Cornbury says goblins are evil anyway. Waluigi taps the projector casing. That detour has established no fact about the thing at the pond. It has established that the investigation begins with people sorting beings into boxes before they know what is in the room. Waluigi labels the first box: NOT YET PROVEN. NO MAP, NO JOBSITE, NO EXTRA DETAIL. The reel keeps moving.

sections.heading: ECTOPLASM, MAGICAL RESIDUE, AND A STORY BY THE POND
sections.body:
Cornbury says the ghosts are hiding, so he cannot lead the party to them. Asked why they would hide, he says they would do so if they had seen him threaten them. Archie points out that Cornbury is standing right in front of the group. Cornbury asks whether he looks scary. Archie says not really; the lion is frightening, not the man, and Cornbury protests that he and the lion are a package deal. Waluigi pauses on that image: one man, one lion, one combined fear product, apparently sold without a label.

The conversation reaches payment. Cornbury says he is paying them and wants ectoplasm as proof that they have subdued the ghosts. Archie asks what they should bring back if the event is not caused by ghosts. Cornbury accepts magical residue instead. Waluigi writes the two requested things in enormous letters: ECTOPLASM OR MAGICAL RESIDUE. The job is to bring back evidence of something supernatural; the evidence has not yet named the source. No, Waluigi will not let a purchase order decide what the phenomenon is.

Asked when he last saw or heard a ghost, Cornbury places the encounter a few hours earlier at the pond. He says he fought it off valiantly, screamed when it appeared, and nearly fell into the water. He repeats that he fought it off, then walks away. Waluigi points at the screen: that is Cornbury's account, not a replay of the encounter. The footage has not shown the claimed fight.

The party now has a location to inspect and a story that can be checked. Waluigi likes this part of the assignment. A witness has identified where, described what he says happened, and left the investigators to compare the account with the ground. He does not like that the desired proof was named before the thing was identified. Those can both be true. Waluigi does not know whether Cornbury is mistaken, exaggerating, or describing something that happened as he says. He can hear the claim; he cannot rewind footage that was never recorded. REQUESTED PROOF IS NOT THE SAME AS AN IDENTIFIED CAUSE. The party heads toward the pond, and Waluigi follows the reel instead of inventing a second camera.

sections.heading: THE AIRSHIP KEYS AND THE FOOTPRINTS IN THE SAND
sections.body:
Before the pond, Rivers asks to be let go and says he wants to return. Remi points out the airship. Markop says someone took its keys; Remi admits she did. She says taking them was for escape, not to take the ship. Markop objects that they cannot simply take somebody else's property. Remi argues that it may be theirs because she woke—or spawned—inside it. Waluigi circles the ownership argument in red, then adds a very large question mark. The account does not settle who owns the airship.

Markop notices X.O.'s powerful staff in Archie's hands and warns him to be careful because it can be wild. Archie says that is why he is holding it and that it is safe with him. Waluigi zooms in on the staff. He can see it. He cannot see a guarantee. The screen carries on, and the party reaches the shoreline: Markop finds footprints in the sand, while Archie and Markop climb down the rocks; Rivers is nearby and Remi stays on the bridge.

Markop says he sees nothing. Archie thinks the tracks suggest a large splash. The water is clear, and Archie notices signs that someone went face-first into it. Markop guesses Cornbury may have fallen into the pond rather than fought a ghost. Waluigi stops the tape on the word MAY. That is an interpretation of the traces, not proof of who entered the water or how. The footprints challenge Cornbury's story; they do not explain the whole scene.

Remi leans over the railing and spots smaller floating spirits, which she calls shiny. Archie tells her to stop drawing their attention. Then everyone notices a much larger apparition that had been floating there unseen. Waluigi leans toward the projector. There it is: something visible at the pond, at last. The image is ghostlike, and the smaller spirits are present too. But a shape is not a diagnosis. Waluigi will not stamp GHOST across the screen just because the picture arrived wearing the right fog. The party has moved from a witness's report to an encounter of its own, and the new question is what that apparition is and what it wants. A FOOTPRINT IS NOT A WITNESS. A SPLASH IS NOT A GHOST.

sections.heading: THE APPARITION WANTS A PURE SOUL AND RIVERS VOLUNTEERS
sections.body:
The apparition calls for Rivers. It says he is a pure soul and that it wants him. Asked why, it repeats that he is a pure soul; it also says something about him leading the ghosts and refers to a chain, without making the explanation clear. Waluigi taps pause. The screen has supplied a demand and a few pieces of language, not a full explanation of the being's purpose. He writes “pure soul” on the margin and refuses to add a definition the scene has not given him.

Rivers immediately offers to be a valiant sacrifice and asks to be released. Archie wants to know what Rivers's angle is when the offered fate could be horrific. Rivers insists there are no tricks or games and that he is simply a good person. Waluigi turns to the audience. Rivers is asking to be untied while offering himself to an unknown thing for an unknown reason. Those two actions occupy the same frame. Waluigi is not going to pick one and crop out the other.

Markop uses Detect Magic. The reading identifies the large apparition as an air elemental. Waluigi clicks the projector remote twice: the first label was ghost-shaped; the magical identification says air elemental. That is a meaningful correction about what the party is facing. It does not explain why the elemental wants Rivers, whether the smaller spirits are connected, or what the words about a chain mean. Archie wonders whether a ghost can use wind attacks, but the group's actual reading has now named an elemental. Waluigi puts the new information on screen without pretending it answers every question. IDENTIFICATION, NOT MOTIVE. A LABEL, NOT A BACKSTORY.

Before the exchange can settle, a Toad appears. He says he has come to save the day, suggests the group may have caught him, and tells Rivers they are coming back for him. Markop says they may have to arrest the newcomer and asks why he wants to help Rivers. The Toad says Rivers is cool and is their leader. Archie tells him Rivers has been lying to him. Waluigi can feel the projector warming under his hand. Another claim has entered the pond scene, and nobody has yet shown its foundation.

sections.heading: THE TOAD THINKS IT IS SPEAKER L AND THE PARTY HAS RIVERS
sections.body:
The newcomer says the group attacked first and threatens to arrest them. He says he thought they were kidnapping Speaker L. Archie realizes the Toad is from another plane, which may explain the mistaken identification; the account does not identify that plane or the Toad himself. Waluigi pulls up a title card reading WRONG SPEAKER? and leaves the question mark where it belongs. The newcomer speaks of Speaker L while the party is holding Speaker Rivers. The apparent confusion is important. The cause of it is still unknown.

Markop prepares for a fight. Archie tells the Toad they are not going to kill Rivers and that he will remain with them for a while. The Toad asks what they want from him. Markop says they have to arrest him—or he can admit his crime and they will leave. Markop calls it just a park and presses him to admit it. The Toad says he cannot have Rivers back. Waluigi holds up both hands. We have an accusation, a proposed arrest, a denial-by-refusal, and a demand to take Rivers. The account does not tell us what crime Markop means or why the Toad thinks Rivers belongs to him. No courtroom has magically appeared in the shrubbery.

Archie pulls Rivers to a tree and uses the rope already around him to tie him there again. Rivers complains that it is prickly. Archie double-ties him. Markop and Archie prepare for a confrontation; Remi is still on the bridge, and the unknown Toad is nearby. Then the air elemental blasts Markop in the face with wind and injures him. Waluigi makes a small involuntary noise at the word face. The argument has become physical before anyone has sorted out the identity problem.

And now Rivers secretly works himself free. He keeps his hands behind his back and pretends the rope still holds him. From Markop's view, Rivers appears tied. Waluigi freezes the frame. Markop is looking at the scene as if the restraint is still there; the audience has seen the hidden movement. Waluigi does not announce an escape. The rope has been defeated, but Rivers has not been shown leaving the scene. That distinction is going to matter in exactly one section, and Waluigi already knows which one. WRONG NAME, UNKNOWN REASON, UNKNOWN MAN.

sections.heading: THE BOLT COMES BACK AND THE ROPE IS STILL A LIE
sections.body:
The Toad shouts about a ghost. Remi fires her crossbow at the apparition; the bolt passes through the air elemental and whips back toward her. Waluigi flinches in his chair and points at the screen: projectile, wind, return trip. That shot has not solved the problem. Archie casts a fire bolt. The elemental says they can talk it out. Waluigi taps the phrase “talk it out” on the glass. That offer is real; it does not erase the wind attack that just injured Markop, and it does not guarantee that the party accepts.

Archie asks whether the elemental still wants Rivers and argues that a conjured being from another plane could switch sides. The elemental blows around them and tells Archie and his “little horse friend” to disengage, promising to spare them. Waluigi rewinds three seconds, not because the words are unclear but because they are doing two things at once: a warning to back off and an offer to spare them. Archie calls to the Toad not to run away because they are still talking to him. The Toad screams as more ghosts appear. The screen is filling up with entities, arguments, wind, and one man standing behind his own hands.

Rivers still looks tied from Markop's view, though the audience knows the rope has been secretly undone. Remi's bolt has not stopped the elemental. Archie's fire bolt has not resolved the exchange. The elemental's offer has not ended the fight, and the newcomer has not been identified. Waluigi starts to reach for the next-reel button. There is no next reel in this account.

All right. Waluigi will concede one physical fact: the magic reading did identify an air elemental, and the crossbow bolt really did pass through it and return toward Remi. The scene is not simply the party mistaking an ordinary person for a ghost. That is the evidence. Waluigi snaps back to the projector before anybody can call that a solution. The additional spirits are appearing, the parties are still together, and Rivers is quietly free of the rope while pretending otherwise. The picture cuts with the encounter unfinished. No exorcism, arrest, rescue, or completed escape appears after it. NO VICTORY CARD. NO RESOLUTION. NO NEXT REEL. WAH!
